sections.title: Interventions
sections.html:
Interventions

The interventions below are host-directed adjuncts intended to be added to standard multidrug anti-tuberculosis chemotherapy (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol or the appropriate drug-resistant regimen). None is a substitute for chemotherapy, and none should be used to delay or de-intensify it. Each candidate is evaluated with the Triangle Test, which asks three questions about an intervention (I) acting on a host feature (f) to affect tuberculosis (D): does I move f in the predicted direction (I→f); does I improve TB clinically (I→D); and is f causally linked to TB (f→D)? Candidates are then classified as Validated (all three edges supported, no contradictions, acceptable safety), Promising Candidate (two of three edges, gaps flagged), or Validation In Progress (mechanistic logic sound, clinical evidence incomplete).

N-acetylcysteine (NAC) — (Promising Candidate)

Feature f: replenishment of intracellular glutathione and host redox balance, plus direct antimycobacterial activity. The triangle edges:

  • I→f (strong, RCT): In a 140-patient randomized controlled trial, adjunctive NAC 1200 mg twice daily significantly raised whole-blood glutathione versus standard therapy alone, confirming target engagement {{cite:wallis2024}}. NAC also exhibits direct, dose-dependent killing of M. tuberculosis in vitro and reduces lung bacillary loads in mice, an effect independent of the host NADPH-oxidase system {{cite:amaral2016}}.
  • f→D (supported): Glutathione depletion and oxidative stress accompany active TB and contribute to immunopathology, and restoring redox balance is mechanistically linked to reduced tissue damage {{cite:amaral2016}}.
  • I→D (mixed): The same RCT found no acceleration of sputum culture conversion (hazard ratio 0.84, 95% CI 0.59–1.20), but did show modest improvement in lung-function recovery (FVC and FEV1), greatest in patients with severe baseline impairment {{cite:wallis2024}}. An earlier phase II trial in HIV-associated TB found NAC safe but underpowered to show a culture-conversion effect {{cite:safe2020}}. A systematic review concluded benefits are plausible but clinically unproven for bacterial clearance {{cite:nacreview2022}}.

Classification: Promising Candidate. Target engagement and mechanism are firmly established, and there is a clinical signal for lung-function preservation, but the predicted bactericidal benefit did not materialize in the pivotal RCT — the I→D edge for sputum conversion is contradicted.

Vitamin D — (Promising Candidate)

Feature f: induction of the antimicrobial peptide cathelicidin (LL-37) and enhancement of macrophage autophagy and phagolysosomal fusion. The triangle edges:

  • f→D (strong): 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D drives vitamin-D-receptor-dependent cathelicidin expression and autophagy, established pathways for macrophage restriction of intracellular M. tuberculosis {{cite:jolliffe2019}}.
  • I→f (supported): Supplementation reliably raises serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and, in deficient hosts, restores cathelicidin-supporting status {{cite:jolliffe2019}}.
  • I→D (mixed/conditional, IPD meta-analysis): An individual-participant-data meta-analysis of 1,850 patients across eight RCTs found no effect on time to sputum culture conversion overall, but a marked acceleration in patients with multidrug-resistant TB (adjusted HR 13.44, 95% CI 2.96–60.90) and a modest acceleration of smear conversion overall {{cite:jolliffe2019}}.

Classification: Promising Candidate. Mechanism (f→D) and target engagement (I→f) are well supported, and a clinically meaningful I→D benefit exists but is restricted to a subgroup (MDR-TB) rather than unselected patients. Benefit is most plausible in baseline deficiency or drug-resistant disease.

Lactoferrin — (Validation In Progress)

Feature f: reinforcement of iron-withholding ("nutritional immunity") to starve M. tuberculosis of iron, plus immunomodulation toward protective Th1 responses with reduced granulomatous immunopathology. The triangle edges:

  • f→D (supported): Iron is essential for mycobacterial growth, and host iron sequestration is a recognized antimycobacterial defense; lactoferrin is a central iron-binding effector of this system {{cite:actor2015}}.
  • I→f (preclinical): In mouse models, oral lactoferrin shifts responses toward CD4+ IFN-γ and IL-17 production while producing fewer, smaller granulomas, and augments BCG vaccine efficacy {{cite:actor2015}}.
  • I→D (not yet established in humans): Clinical efficacy data in TB patients are lacking; the evidence base is confined to murine and in vitro studies {{cite:actor2015}}.

Classification: Validation In Progress. The mechanistic logic is coherent and preclinical data are encouraging, but there are no human treatment trials demonstrating an I→D effect.

Arginine / nitric oxide — (Promising Candidate)

Feature f: provision of L-arginine as substrate for inducible nitric oxide synthase, enabling macrophage nitric-oxide-mediated killing of M. tuberculosis. The triangle edges:

  • f→D (supported): Nitric oxide is a recognized mycobactericidal effector of activated macrophages, and arginine is its rate-limiting substrate {{cite:schon2003}}.
  • I→D (mixed, RCTs): An early double-blind RCT (n=120) reported faster sputum conversion, greater weight gain, and faster symptom resolution with adjunctive arginine in HIV-negative patients {{cite:schon2003}}. However, a larger randomized, placebo-controlled trial (n=200) of L-arginine 6 g/day found no effect on week-4 culture conversion or clinical severity, though it was underpowered {{cite:ralph2013}}. A peanut-based (arginine-rich) food trial in Ethiopia showed no overall benefit but improved cure rates in HIV-positive patients {{cite:mily2013}}.
  • I→f (uncertain): The negative trial found no increase in fractional exhaled nitric oxide with supplementation, raising doubt about whether oral arginine reliably augments NO output at the infection site {{cite:ralph2013}}.

Classification: Promising Candidate. The f→D rationale is strong and one RCT is positive, but target engagement (I→f) is unconfirmed and the larger trial was null; benefit may be confined to specific subgroups (e.g., HIV-negative or HIV-positive depending on study).
